docs.text: Loom Studio is a built-in control plane for your agents. It provides a real-time visualization layer on top of your telemetry data.

docs.title: Running Loom Studio
docs.text:
To start Loom Studio, run:

loom studio

By default, it will: - Open a web dashboard on http://localhost:8080. - Listen for OTLP gRPC telemetry on localhost:4317. - Listen for OTLP HTTP telemetry on localhost:4318. - Store data in a local SQLite database at .loom/telemetry.db.

docs.title: Core Views
docs.text:
1. Dashboard: A high-level overview of system health, featuring token consumption, LLM call volume, P50 latency, and tool invocation counts.
  2. Trace Explorer: An audit log of every execution thread. You can search by Thread ID or Graph name to find specific interactions.
  3. Trace Waterfall: A detailed Gantt-style view of a single execution. It breaks down the timing of every LLM call, node transition, and tool execution.
  4. Metrics Explorer: A deep-dive into time-series data. It supports Temporal Bucketing (1s to 1h intervals) to smooth out data and ensure fast rendering even with millions of points.

docs.title: Semantic Conventions (v1.41.1)
docs.text: Loom strictly adheres to the latest OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions. This means spans and metrics are standardized: - Inference Spans: Named chat {model} with attributes for tokens (input/output/reasoning/cache), temperature, and response IDs. - Tool Spans: Named execute_tool {name}. - Histograms: Use the official explicit bucket boundaries for precise distribution analysis.

docs.title: Automatic Tracing
docs.text: Loom's Model and Graph packages automatically emit OpenTelemetry spans and metrics for: - LLM requests (using GenAI semantic conventions). - Node entry and exit. - Graph execution durations and node invocations.

docs.title: Capturing Sensitive Content
docs.text:
By default, Loom does not record sensitive content (prompts, completion text, tool results) to protect your privacy. You can opt-in to content recording using telemetry.WithContentRecording:

ctx = telemetry.WithContentRecording(ctx)
// Subsequent LLM and tool calls in this context will record their payloads

docs.title: Production Observability
docs.text:
Since Loom uses standard OpenTelemetry under the hood, you can easily point it to any OTel-compliant backend (Datadog, Honeycomb, Jaeger, etc.) by setting the standard environment variables:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="https://api.honeycomb.io"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="x-honeycomb-team=your-api-key"

If your application already has OpenTelemetry configured, Loom will automatically use your existing TracerProvider and MeterProvider without any additional setup.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Trace IDs: Always propagate context.Context through your application to ensure spans are correctly parented.
  • Attributes: Use standard semantic conventions for custom attributes when possible to ensure compatibility with various observability tools.
  • Sampling: In high-throughput production environments, consider configuring a sampler to reduce the volume of telemetry data.

docs.title: Persistence & State 💾
docs.text: One of Loom's core strengths is its "state-first" architecture. Every time a node executes, Loom saves a checkpoint of your workflow's state. This allows you to resume execution after a failure, restart a long-running process, audit execution history, or pause a graph to wait for human input.

docs.title: How Checkpointing Works
docs.text:
Loom uses a Checkpointer interface to persist snapshots of the State. A snapshot includes: - The current values in your state struct decomposed into channel keys. - The execution history and next nodes to run. - The Location (ThreadID, CheckpointNS, CheckpointID) for resumption.

type Checkpointer interface {
    Load(context.Context, Location) (*Checkpoint, error)
    Record(context.Context, Checkpoint) error
}

docs.title: Default: graph.NoopCheckpointer
docs.text: If you do not configure a checkpointer via builder.WithCheckpointer(...), Loom automatically defaults to graph.NoopCheckpointer{}: - Load always returns nil, nil. - Record is an instantaneous no-op. - Graphs run fully in-memory with zero disk or database overhead, while retaining identical execution semantics.

docs.title: 1. Setting up a Checkpointer
docs.text: Loom provides production-ready checkpointers for SQLite and PostgreSQL.

docs.title: SQLite
docs.text:
import (
    "database/sql"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/checkpoint/sqlite"
    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

db, err := sql.Open("sqlite3", "loom.db")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

cp, err := sqlite.NewCheckpointer(db)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Attach to the graph builder
builder.WithCheckpointer(cp)

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
The PostgreSQL checkpointer uses an efficient three-table schema (checkpoints, checkpoint_blobs, and checkpoint_writes) with content-addressable deduplication. pg.NewCheckpointer accepts an initialized *sql.DB:

import (
    "database/sql"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/checkpoint/pg"
    _ "github.com/lib/pq"
)

db, err := sql.Open("postgres", "postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/loom?sslmode=disable")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// NewCheckpointer automatically executes pending migrations
cp, err := pg.NewCheckpointer(db)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

builder.WithCheckpointer(cp)

docs.title: 2. Checkpoint Locations, Pre-Minted IDs & Deterministic Task IDs
Pre-Minted Checkpoint IDs
docs.text: Before executing any step's nodes, Loom pre-mints a time-ordered UUIDv7 CheckpointID and passes it inside the execution location. This ensures: - Nodes know the upcoming checkpoint ID in advance. - Telemetry spans, events, and writes are tied to the exact checkpoint before it is written. - Inspecting graph.RuntimeFromContext(ctx) exposes: - rt.RunID (the pre-minted CheckpointID) - rt.Step (current zero-based step index) - rt.NodeName (name of the executing node) - rt.Location (ThreadID, CheckpointNS, CheckpointID)

docs.title: Deterministic TaskID
docs.text:
For every node invocation, Loom derives a deterministic TaskID using SHA-1 over (ThreadID, CheckpointNS, Step, NodeName):

taskID := computeTaskID(threadID, checkpointNS, step, nodeName)

This predictable identity guarantees idempotency and enables safe correlation between node writes and checkpoint states.

docs.title: 3. Hierarchical Subgraph Namespaces
docs.text:
When embedding sub-graphs via childGraph.AsNode() or graph.MapNode(), child checkpoints are stored within a segmented, hierarchical namespace modeled after LangGraph:

$$\text{CheckpointNS} = \langle\text{parent_ns}\rangle \mid \langle\text{node_name}\rangle:\langle\text{task_id}\rangle$$

Where: - | (NSSep) separates nesting levels. - : (NSEnd) separates the node name from its deterministic task ID.

docs.title: Example Namespace Hierarchy:
docs.text:
• Root Graph: "" (empty string)
  • Child Subgraph Node named "researcher": "researcher:4f8a12bc..."
  • Nested Child Subgraph Node named "web_search": "researcher:4f8a12bc...|web_search:9c2d34ef..."

docs.title: Key Namespace Properties:
docs.text:
1. Resume Stability: When an interrupt occurs inside a sub-graph, the execution step counter is preserved. When resumed, the child sub-graph receives the exact same CheckpointNS and resumes directly from its paused state.
  2. Loop Isolation: When a graph loops back to a node across distinct execution steps, the incremented step counter generates a distinct TaskID, preventing namespace collision between iterations.
  3. Node Name Restrictions: Because | and : are reserved delimiters for namespace segmentation, node names must not contain | or :. Slashes (e.g., "search/web", "agent/writer") and standard alphanumeric characters are permitted.

docs.title: Pausing with graph.Interrupt or graph.InterruptUpdate
docs.text:
You can pause a graph's execution using graph.Interrupt() or graph.InterruptUpdate[S](). Loom immediately stops execution, persists the state to durable storage, and returns the snapshot:

builder.AddNode("Approval", graph.NodeFunc[MyState](func(ctx context.Context, s MyState) (graph.Command[MyState], error) {
    if !s.IsApproved {
        // Stop execution and save checkpoint
        return graph.Interrupt(), nil 
    }
    return graph.Update[MyState](func(s MyState) MyState { return s }), nil
}))

docs.title: Resuming from a Checkpoint
docs.text:
When a graph is interrupted or finishes, it returns a Snapshot[State]. You can resume execution from the returned snapshot.Location by providing the resume location to Execute:

// 1. Initial execution
snapshot, err := g.Execute(ctx, initialCmd, &graph.Location{ThreadID: "order-1234"})
threadID := snapshot.Location.ThreadID

// ... Later (e.g. human approves the order via HTTP webhook) ...

// 2. Resume using the thread's last checkpoint location
resumeLocation := &graph.Location{
    ThreadID:     threadID,
    CheckpointNS: snapshot.Location.CheckpointNS,
}

approvalUpdate := graph.Update[MyState](func(s MyState) MyState {
    s.IsApproved = true
    return s
})

resumedSnapshot, err := g.Execute(ctx, approvalUpdate, resumeLocation)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• State Serialization: Ensure all fields in your state struct have appropriate JSON tags.
  • Thread Management: Use unique ThreadIDs to isolate different user sessions or independent tasks.
  • Idempotency: Since a node might be re-executed upon retry or resumption, ensure node functions are idempotent.
  • Sub-graph Hygiene: Avoid using | or : in node names to prevent namespace delimiter conflicts.

docs.title: Persistent Store 💾
docs.text: The store package provides a namespaced key-value store for persistent, searchable long-term memory. It gives AI agents the ability to read and write structured data that survives across graph executions, process restarts, and conversations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The store follows a clean interface pattern: a core Store interface in the parent package, with backend implementations in sub-packages. All values are JSON-serialized internally — callers pass Go pointers and the store marshals/unmarshals automatically.

store/
├── store.go        # Core Store interface
├── options.go      # Variadic options (PutOption, SearchOption, etc.)
├── index.go        # Semantic indexing (IndexConfig, Embedder, vector helpers)
├── context.go      # WithStore / FromContext integration
├── generic.go      # Generic helpers: Get[T], Search[T]
├── memorydb/       # In-memory backend (dev / testing)
├── sqlite/         # SQLite backend (pure-Go vector search via scalar function)
└── pg/             # PostgreSQL backend (pgvector HNSW similarity search)

docs.title: Core Interface
docs.text:
The Store interface exposes four operations over a namespace/key address space:

Method Purpose Put Marshal value to JSON and store it under namespace/key. Upserts if the key exists. Get Retrieve a single item by namespace/key and unmarshal into a pointer. Returns store.ErrNotFound if missing. Search Find items within a namespace. Supports filtering by prefix, semantic query (WithQuery), limit, and offset. Delete Remove an item. Idempotent — returns nil if the key does not exist.

docs.title: GORM-Style API
docs.text:
The API follows the GORM / json.Unmarshal pattern: callers pass a pointer and the store populates it. No json.RawMessage leaks into the public API.

s := store.FromContext(ctx)

var prefs UserPrefs
if err := s.Get(ctx, "user:123", "preferences", &prefs); err != nil { ... }

docs.title: Generic Package-Level Helpers
docs.text:
For callers who prefer typed returns over pointer passing:

memories, err := store.Get[Memories](ctx, s, "user:123", "memories")

items, err := store.Search[Item](ctx, s, "user:123", store.WithLimit(10))

docs.title: In-Memory Backend (Development)
docs.text:
The memorydb backend is a zero-dependency, concurrent-safe in-memory store. Ideal for development, testing, and unit tests.

import "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/store/memorydb"

s := memorydb.New()
builder.WithStore(s)

docs.title: SQLite Backend (Single-Node Production)
docs.text:
The sqlite backend persists namespaced key-value data to a store_items table, enabling durable long-term memory across process restarts with zero CGO dependencies.

import (
    "database/sql"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/store/sqlite"
    _ "modernc.org/sqlite"
)

db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "loom.db")
if err != nil { ... }

s, err := sqlite.NewStore(db)
if err != nil { ... }

builder.WithStore(s)

docs.title: PostgreSQL Backend (Distributed Production)
docs.text:
The pg backend persists items in PostgreSQL using JSONB (and pgvector with an HNSW index when semantic search is configured).

import (
    "database/sql"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/store/pg"
    _ "github.com/lib/pq"
)

db, err := sql.Open("postgres", os.Getenv("POSTGRES_DSN"))
if err != nil { ... }

s, err := pg.NewStore(db)
if err != nil { ... }

builder.WithStore(s)

docs.title: Semantic Vector Search
docs.text:
All three store backends (memorydb, sqlite, and pg) support automatic semantic indexing and similarity search. Pass a store.IndexConfig when constructing the store:

import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/embedding"
    loomopenai "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/openai"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/store"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/store/memorydb"
)

provider, _ := loomopenai.NewDefaultProvider()
embedModel, _ := embedding.NewModel(provider, "text-embedding-3-small", nil)

// Initialize the store with semantic search
s := memorydb.New(memorydb.WithIndex(store.IndexConfig{
    Embed:  embedModel,
    Dims:   1536,             // Optional if embedModel has profile/configured dimensions
    Fields: []string{"text"}, // gjson field paths to vectorize (empty embeds whole payload)
}))

type Document struct {
    Text string `json:"text"`
}

// Store an item (automatically embeds the "text" field)
_ = s.Put(ctx, "docs", "doc1", Document{Text: "Python tutorial for agents"})

// Search semantically
results, err := store.Search[Document](ctx, s, "docs",
    store.WithQuery("programming guides"),
    store.WithLimit(5),
)

docs.title: How Each Backend Stores & Searches Embeddings
docs.text: Backend Vector Storage Similarity Engine memorydb embedding.Vector on in-memory entry embedding.Vector.CosineSimilarity sqlite Separate store_embeddings table (embedding BLOB) Registered pure-Go deterministic SQLite scalar function (loom_vec_cosine) pg Separate store_embeddings table (vector(dims)) Native pgvector cosine distance (<=>) with hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) index

docs.title: Per-Put Indexing Controls
docs.text:
You can disable indexing or override indexed gjson field paths for an individual Put call:

// Skip embedding generation for this item
_ = s.Put(ctx, "docs", "raw-config", cfg, store.WithIndexDisabled())

// Embed specific nested fields or array queries for this item
_ = s.Put(ctx, "docs", "article-1", article, store.WithIndexFields("title", "meta.summary", "sections.#.heading"))

docs.title: Retrieving the Store
docs.text:
The store is injected into the context. Retrieve it with store.FromContext:

func myNode(ctx context.Context, s MyState) (graph.Command[MyState], error) {
    store := store.FromContext(ctx)
    if store == nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("store not configured")
    }
    // ...
}

docs.title: Per-User Scoping
docs.text:
Use namespaced keys to isolate data per user, session, or agent:

s := store.FromContext(ctx)

// Per-user preferences
ns := fmt.Sprintf("%s:user-data", userID)
var prefs UserPrefs
if err := s.Get(ctx, ns, "preferences", &prefs); err != nil { ... }

// Per-agent knowledge
ns = fmt.Sprintf("%s:knowledge", agentID)
s.Put(ctx, ns, "latest-finding", result)

docs.title: Inside a Graph Node
docs.text:
func myNode(ctx context.Context, s MyState) (graph.Command[MyState], error) {
    store := store.FromContext(ctx)

    // GORM-style
    var prefs UserPrefs
    err := s.Get(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("%s:user-data", s.UserID), "preferences", &prefs)

    // Generic-style
    memories, err := store.Get[Memories](ctx, store, fmt.Sprintf("%s:user-data", s.UserID), "memories")

    return graph.Update(func(s MyState) MyState { return s }), nil
}

docs.title: Inside a Tool
docs.text:
func myTool(ctx context.Context, args MyArgs) (string, error) {
    s := store.FromContext(ctx)
    if err := s.Put(ctx, "agent:knowledge", "latest-finding", result); err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    return "saved", nil
}

docs.title: Search Options
docs.text:
The Search method supports variadic options for filtering, semantic search, and pagination:

Option Purpose WithQuery(query) Rank results by semantic similarity to query WithKeyPrefix(prefix) Filter results to keys matching the given prefix WithLimit(n) Cap the number of items returned WithOffset(n) Skip the first N items (pagination) 
var items []Item
err := s.Search(ctx, "user:123", &items,
    store.WithKeyPrefix("mem:"),
    store.WithQuery("recent project deadlines"),
    store.WithLimit(10),
    store.WithOffset(0),
)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Namespace Convention: Use hierarchical namespace strings for logical grouping, e.g., "user:123:data" or "agent:knowledge".
  • Thread Safety: All backends are safe for concurrent use — memorydb uses sync.RWMutex, while sqlite and pg rely on sql.DB connection pooling.
  • Idempotency: Delete is idempotent (returns nil for missing keys). Design node functions to be idempotent where possible, since retries may occur.
  • JSON Serialization: All values are JSON-serialized. Ensure struct fields are JSON-serializable.
  • Backend Selection: Use memorydb for development and unit tests, sqlite for single-node deployments (up to ~50k–100k vectors per namespace), and pg with pgvector for large-scale or multi-instance production deployments.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide 🧵
docs.text: Welcome to Loom! This guide will help you build your first graph-based AI agent. Loom allows you to define complex AI workflows as directed graphs, making it easy to manage state, branching logic, and persistence.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
Before we dive into the code, let's look at the three main building blocks of Loom:

  1. State: A Go struct that holds all the data for your workflow.
  2. Nodes: Functions that perform work and update the state.
  3. Edges: The connections between nodes that define the flow of execution.

docs.title: 1. Define Your State
docs.text:
Every Loom graph operates on a shared state. This state must implement a Copy() method to ensure that each step in the graph works on an independent snapshot.

type AppState struct {
    Input    string `json:"input"`
    Category string `json:"category"`
    Output   string `json:"output"`
}

func (s AppState) Copy() AppState {
    return s
}

docs.title: 2. Initialize the Graph Builder
docs.text:
The graph.Builder is used to assemble your nodes and edges.

builder := graph.New[AppState]()

docs.title: 3. Add Nodes
docs.text:
Nodes are where the logic happens. A node takes the current state and returns a Command, which tells the Loom engine how to update the state or where to go next. Wrap node functions with graph.NodeFunc[State] to implement graph.Node[State]:

builder.AddNode("Categorize", graph.NodeFunc[AppState](func(ctx context.Context, state AppState) (graph.Command[AppState], error) {
    category := "general"
    if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(state.Input), "math") {
        category = "math"
    }

    // Return an Update command to modify the state
    return graph.Update[AppState](func(s AppState) AppState {
        s.Category = category
        return s
    }), nil
}))

docs.title: 4. Define the Workflow (Edges)
docs.text:
Edges connect your nodes. Loom supports direct edges and Route Edges for conditional branching.

// Start at the Categorize node
builder.AddEdge(graph.START, "Categorize")

// Branch based on the 'Category' in the state
builder.AddRouteEdge("Categorize", func(s AppState) (string, error) {
    return s.Category, nil
}, map[string]string{
    "math":    "MathLLM",
    "general": "GeneralLLM",
})

// Both branches lead to the END node
builder.AddEdge("MathLLM", graph.END)
builder.AddEdge("GeneralLLM", graph.END)

docs.title: 5. Build and Execute
docs.text:
Once your graph is defined, you can build it and execute it with an initial input.

g, _ := builder.Build()

// Execute the graph
initialState := AppState{Input: "What is 2+2?"}
snapshot, _ := g.Execute(ctx, graph.Update[AppState](func(s AppState) AppState {
    return initialState
}), nil)

fmt.Println("Final Output:", snapshot.State.Output)

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Now that you've built your first graph, check out these advanced guides:

  • Graph Workflows: Deep dive into parallel fan-out/fan-in, sub-graphs (AsNode/MapNode), node middleware, retries, and execution safety.
  • Conversations: Deep dive into message roles, multimodal content, and history.
  • LLM Package: Deep dive into the Model API and Registry.
  • LLM Providers: Learn about OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Ollama.
  • Persistence & State: Learn how to save and resume your workflows.
  • Human-in-the-Loop: Patterns for human approval and input.
  • Tools & Streaming: Integrate your agents with external tools and real-time updates.
  • Memory Management: Handle long conversations with automated trimming and summarization.
  • Observability: Visualize your graphs and trace execution.
  • Custom Providers: (Advanced) How to add support for new LLM backends.

docs.title: Documents, Vector Stores & Retrievers (RAG) 📚
docs.text:
Loom provides a modular, end-to-end Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline built around three focused packages:

  1. document (github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/document) — Document, lazy iterator Loader implementations, and text Splitter chunkers (RecursiveCharacterSplitter, MarkdownSplitter).
  2. vectorstore (github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/vectorstore) — VectorStore interface and backends (memory, sqlite, pg) for batch embedding, similarity search, and metadata filtering.
  3. retriever (github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/retriever) — Retriever runtime interface with OpenTelemetry spans, on_retrieve stream events, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (NewMerger), System One decision reranking (NewDecisionReranker), and agent tool integration (NewTool).
flowchart LR
    A["Loader<br/>(FS, CSV, JSON, Reader)"] -->|iter.Seq2| B["Splitter<br/>(Recursive, Markdown)"]
    B -->|[]Document chunks| C["VectorStore<br/>(memory, sqlite, pg)"]
    D["Query"] --> E["Retriever<br/>(Vector, RRF, DecisionReranker)"]
    C <-->|Top-K + Filter| E
    E -->|[]Document| F["Graph Node / Agent Tool"]

docs.title: 1. Loading Documents (document.Loader)
docs.text:
Every loader in document implements a single-method lazy iterator interface using Go's iter.Seq2[Document, error]:

type Loader interface {
    Load(ctx context.Context) iter.Seq2[Document, error]
}

docs.title: Built-in Loaders
docs.text:
Loader Constructor Description TextLoader document.NewTextLoader(text, meta...) Wraps an in-memory string as a Document. ReaderLoader document.NewReaderLoader(r, source, meta...) Reads any io.Reader into a single Document. FSLoader document.NewFSLoader(fsys, patterns...) Lazily walks an fs.FS (e.g. os.DirFS, embed.FS) matching glob patterns and populates source, path, name, ext metadata. CSVLoader document.NewCSVLoader(r, opts...) Streams CSV rows lazily (WithCSVSource, WithCSVContentColumns, WithCSVDelimiter). JSONLoader document.NewJSONLoader(r, opts...) Streams JSON arrays, objects, or JSONL (WithJSONLines(true), WithJSONContentKey). HTMLLoader document.NewHTMLLoader(r, opts...) Parses HTML DOM via golang.org/x/net/html, extracts <title> and <meta name="description">, and strips <script>/<style>/boilerplate tags. 
import (
    "context"
    "os"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/document"
)

ctx := context.Background()

// Lazily walk all Markdown files in ./docs
loader := document.NewFSLoader(os.DirFS("./docs"), "*.md")

// Materialize into a slice when needed:
docs, err := document.LoadAll(ctx, loader)

docs.title: 2. Splitting Documents (document.Splitter)
docs.text: Large documents should be split into smaller, overlapping chunks before embedding so that retrieved passages stay focused and fit comfortably in the model's context window.

docs.title: Recursive Character Splitter
docs.text:
Splits text hierarchically by ["\n\n", "\n", " ", ""] to keep paragraphs and sentences intact:

splitter := document.NewRecursiveCharacterSplitter(
    document.WithChunkSize(1000),
    document.WithChunkOverlap(200),
)

chunks := splitter.SplitDocuments(docs)

docs.title: Markdown Splitter
docs.text:
Splits Markdown by headings (#–######), records active section headings in each chunk's Metadata ("h1", "h2", etc.), and keeps fenced code blocks intact:

mdSplitter := document.NewMarkdownSplitter(
    document.WithChunkSize(800),
    document.WithChunkOverlap(100),
)

// Stream lazily from Loader -> Splitter without loading all files into memory at once:
for chunk, err := range document.SplitIter(loader.Load(ctx), mdSplitter) {
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    // chunk.Metadata["h1"], chunk.Metadata["chunk_index"], chunk.Metadata["parent_id"]
}

docs.title: 3. Indexing & Searching (vectorstore.VectorStore)
docs.text: vectorstore.VectorStore embeds batches of documents via embedding.Model.EmbedDocuments and searches them by cosine similarity.

docs.title: Choosing a Backend
docs.text:
In-Memory (vectorstore/memory)SQLite (vectorstore/sqlite)PostgreSQL pgvector (vectorstore/pg) 
import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/vectorstore/memory"
)

vs := memory.New(embedModel)

import (
    "database/sql"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/vectorstore/sqlite"
    _ "modernc.org/sqlite"
)

db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "vectors.db")
vs, err := sqlite.New(db, embedModel)

import (
    "database/sql"
    _ "github.com/lib/pq"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/vectorstore/pg"
)

db, _ := sql.Open("postgres", os.Getenv("POSTGRES_DSN"))
vs, err := pg.New(db, embedModel, pg.WithDims(1536))

docs.title: Adding, Searching, and Deleting Documents
docs.text:
// 1. Batch-embed and index chunks
ids, err := vs.Add(ctx, chunks, vectorstore.WithAddNamespace("docs"))

// 2. Similarity search with metadata filter, minimum score, and optional MMR diversification
matches, err := vs.Search(ctx, "How do I resume an interrupted graph?", 5,
    vectorstore.WithNamespace("docs"),
    vectorstore.WithFilter(map[string]any{"ext": ".md"}),
    vectorstore.WithMinScore(0.55),
    vectorstore.WithMMR(0.5, 20), // Balance relevance (0.5) and diversity across top 20 candidates
)

// 3. Delete by ID
_ = vs.Delete(ctx, ids, vectorstore.WithDeleteNamespace("docs"))

docs.title: 4. Composable Retrievers (retriever.Retriever)
docs.text: The retriever package provides a uniform query interface (Retrieve(ctx, query, opts...) ([]document.Document, error)) with built-in OpenTelemetry tracing and on_retrieve stream events.

docs.title: Vector Store Retriever
docs.text:
import "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/retriever"

baseRetriever := retriever.FromVectorStore(vs,
    retriever.WithNamespace("docs"),
    retriever.WithTopK(10),
    retriever.WithMMR(0.6, 30),
)

docs.title: BM25 Lexical Retriever & Reciprocal Rank Fusion (NewBM25 + NewMerger)
docs.text:
Pair BM25Retriever (Okapi BM25 keyword search) with VectorStoreRetriever inside NewMerger for hybrid lexical + semantic search:

bm25Retriever := retriever.NewBM25(chunks)

mergedRetriever := retriever.NewMerger(
    []retriever.Retriever{baseRetriever, bm25Retriever},
    retriever.WithRRFConstant(60),
)

docs.title: System One Decision Reranker (NewDecisionReranker)
docs.text:
Use a fast decision.Model to evaluate each candidate chunk in parallel, discard irrelevant passages below a probability threshold, and sort by calibrated relevance probability:

reranker := retriever.NewDecisionReranker(
    baseRetriever,
    decisionModel,
    "Does this document contain factual information that helps answer the query?",
    retriever.WithThreshold(0.65),
)

topDocs, err := reranker.Retrieve(ctx, "How does SQLite checkpointing work?", retriever.WithTopK(3))

docs.title: Agent Tool Integration (NewTool)
docs.text:
Expose any Retriever directly to an LLM agent as a read-only tool.Tool:

kbTool, err := retriever.NewTool(
    "search_knowledge_base",
    "Search internal documentation for architecture and API usage guides",
    reranker,
    retriever.WithTopK(4),
)

container := tool.NewContainer(kbTool)
chatModel = chatModel.BindToolDefs(container.Definitions()...)

docs.title: 5. End-to-End Example (examples/rag)
docs.text: Loom includes a complete, runnable end-to-end RAG example in examples/rag/main.go. It demonstrates: - Streaming documents lazily with document.NewFSLoader. - Chunking Markdown by heading hierarchy with document.NewMarkdownSplitter. - In-memory vector store indexing (vectorstore/memory) with dense embeddings. - Hybrid lexical (BM25) and semantic retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (retriever.NewMerger). - A stateful RAG graph workflow (retrieve $\to$ generate) using graph.Builder.

docs.title: Running with Ollama (Local)
docs.text:
Ensure Ollama is running and has the required models installed (ollama pull gemma3 and ollama pull nomic-embed-text):

go run ./examples/rag -provider ollama

You can customize the query and models using CLI flags:

go run ./examples/rag -provider ollama -llm-model gemma3 -embed-model nomic-embed-text -query "How does Loom checkpoint graph state?"

docs.title: Running with OpenAI
docs.text:
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
go run ./examples/rag -provider openai -query "How do decision models route graph workflows?"

docs.title: Tools & Streaming 🛠️
docs.text: Tools allow your AI agents to interact with external systems, APIs, and databases. Loom provides a robust, type-safe way to define tools and execute them within your graphs.

docs.title: 1. Defining a Tool
docs.text:
Loom uses Go reflection to automatically generate the JSON schema for your tools, which is then sent to the LLM.

type SearchInput struct {
    Query string `json:"query"`
}

type SearchOutput struct {
    Results []string `json:"results"`
}

searchTool, _ := tool.New(
    "web_search",          // Name
    "Web Search",         // Display Name
    "Searches the web",   // Description
    func(ctx context.Context, in SearchInput) (SearchOutput, error) {
        // Implementation logic
        return SearchOutput{Results: []string{"Result 1"}}, nil
    },
)

docs.title: 2. Using the Tool Container
docs.text:
The tool.Container groups multiple tools together and handles their execution.

container := tool.NewContainer(searchTool, calculatorTool)

// Bind tool definitions to the model
model = model.BindToolDefs(container.Definitions()...)

In a graph node, you can execute a tool call received from the LLM:

resp, err := container.Call(ctx, assistantToolCall)

docs.title: 3. Streaming Tools
docs.text:
Loom supports "Streaming Tools" which can report progress to the UI or yield multiple parts of a result (e.g., text followed by an image).

processorTool, _ := tool.NewStreaming(
    "analyze_data",
    "Data Processor",
    "Analyzes data and returns results",
    func(ctx context.Context, in struct{ Dataset string }) (tool.ToolStream, error) {
        return func(yield func(message.ToolChunk, error) bool) {
            // Report progress
            curr := 1.0; total := 2.0
            yield(message.ToolChunk{
                Progress: "Analyzing...",
                ProgressCurrent: &curr,
                ProgressTotal: &total,
            }, nil)

            // Yield result
            yield(message.ToolChunk{
                Content: message.Content{&message.TextBlock{Text: "Result"}},
            }, nil)
        }, nil
    },
)

docs.title: 4. MCP Tools
docs.text:
Loom provides first-class support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). You can dynamically extract tools from any MCP-compliant server and add them to your tool.Container.

// Connect to an MCP server
client := mcp.NewClient(mcp.Config{
    Transport: "stdio",
    Command:   "python",
    Args:      []string{"my_server.py"},
})
defer client.Close()

// Extract tools as native Loom tools
mcpTools, _ := client.Tools(ctx)

// Integrate with Loom container
container := tool.NewContainer(mcpTools...)

See the MCP Guide for more details.

docs.title: 5. Graph Streaming
docs.text:
To observe tool progress and token-level updates from the LLM, use the g.Stream method.

events, _ := g.Stream(ctx, input, nil)

for event, err := range events {
    // The 'Source' field identifies the origin (e.g., "llm:gpt-4o" or "tool:web_search")
    fmt.Printf("[%s] ", event.Source)

    switch event.Event {
    case graph.EventToolProgress:
        chunk := event.Data.(message.ToolChunk)
        fmt.Println("Progress:", chunk.Progress)
    case graph.EventLLMChunk:
        chunk := event.Data.(message.AssistantChunk)
        fmt.Print(chunk.Content.Text())
    }
}

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• tool.New: For standard request-response tools.
  • tool.NewStreaming: For tools that need to report progress or stream multi-part results.
  • tool.Container: For managing and executing multiple tools.
  • g.Stream: For real-time event monitoring.

docs.title: Anthropic Provider 🔌
docs.text: The Anthropic provider supports the Claude family of models, including Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Haiku.

docs.title: 1. Setup & Authentication
docs.text:
Set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-api-key-here'

docs.title: 2. Basic Usage
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/llm"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/anthropic"
)

provider, err := loomanthropic.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    // handle error
}

model := llm.NewModel(provider, "claude-3-5-sonnet-latest")

docs.title: Thinking (Reasoning) Mode
docs.text:
Anthropic models support a dedicated "thinking" budget for extended reasoning.

model = model.WithThinking(4000) // 4000 tokens for internal reasoning

docs.title: Adaptive Thinking
docs.text:
Enable the model to dynamically adjust its thinking process.

model = model.WithAdaptiveThinking()

docs.title: Prompt Caching
docs.text: Anthropic support "Prompt Caching" via ephemeral markers. Loom provides a structured way to leverage this at two levels:

docs.title: 1. Caching the "Header" (Call Extension)
docs.text:
This is the most common pattern. It caches the static parts of your request (system prompt and tool definitions) so they are reused across turns.

// Use the PromptCaching extension
model = model.WithExtension(loomanthropic.PromptCaching{
    CacheHeader: true,
})

docs.title: 2. Manual Breakpoints (Message Extension)
docs.text:
You can mark specific messages in the conversation as cache checkpoints using Message Extensions.

// Add a breakpoint to this specific turn using the fluent API
msg := message.NewUserText("Analyze this 500-page PDF...").
    WithExtension(&loomanthropic.MessageCache{Enabled: true})

docs.title: 4. Model Catalog
docs.text:
The provider maintains a list of known Anthropic models and their characteristics.

profile, found := provider.GetProfile("claude-3-5-sonnet-latest")
if found {
    fmt.Println("Context Limit:", profile.Limits.Context)
}

docs.title: Google Antigravity Provider 🔌
docs.text: The Google Antigravity provider connects Loom to Google's internal Cloud Code / Antigravity LLM backend, supporting streaming completions, dynamic model discovery, thinking effort configuration, and quota inspection.

docs.title: 1. Setup & Authentication
docs.text: The provider supports three authentication methods:

docs.title: Option A: Interactive Browser OAuth 2.0 PKCE (Recommended)
docs.text:
Automatically runs a local loopback server, requests authorization from Google, securely stores credentials in ~/.config/loom/antigravity_token.json, and handles background token refresh:

import "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/antigravity"

oauthProvider, err := loomantigravity.NewOAuth2TokenProvider(loomantigravity.OAuth2Config{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Interactively log in if no token is saved
if err := oauthProvider.Login(ctx); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

Or authenticate via the example CLI tool: 

go run ./examples/antigravity --login

docs.title: Option B: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Export a valid bearer token: 

export ANTIGRAVITY_TOKEN="<your-oauth-bearer-token>"
# or
export GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN="<your-oauth-bearer-token>"
The provider will automatically pick up ANTIGRAVITY_TOKEN or GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN.

docs.title: Option C: Static Token
docs.text:
Pass an existing token programmatically: 

tokenProvider := loomantigravity.StaticToken("<your-oauth-bearer-token>")

docs.title: 2. Basic Usage
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/llm"
    loomantigravity "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/antigravity"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/message"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // 1. Initialize provider
    provider, err := loomantigravity.NewDefaultProvider()
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // 2. Instantiate model (e.g. Gemini 3.8 Flash)
    model := llm.NewModel(provider, "gemini-3.8-flash")

    // 3. Stream a completion
    stream, err := model.Stream(ctx, message.MessageList{
        message.NewUserText("Explain quantum computing in three sentences."),
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    for chunk, err := range stream {
        if err != nil {
            log.Fatal(err)
        }
        fmt.Print(chunk.Content.Text())
    }
    fmt.Println()
}

docs.title: Thinking & Reasoning Effort
docs.text:
Antigravity models support configurable thinking budgets and levels (low, medium, high):

// 1. Via fluent Model configuration
model = model.WithThinkingEffort("high")

// 2. Or using dynamic model alias names
fastModel := llm.NewModel(provider, "gemini-3.8-flash-low")
deepModel := llm.NewModel(provider, "gemini-3.8-flash-high")

The provider's heuristic resolver automatically sets thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel = "HIGH" and routes requests to the underlying gateway endpoint (such as gemini-3.8-flash-tiered).

docs.title: Dynamic Model Discovery & Resolution
docs.text:
Antigravity discovers available models dynamically at runtime directly from Google's /v1internal:fetchAvailableModels endpoint:

  • Zero hardcoded catalogs: Newly published models (e.g. Gemini 3.9, Claude updates) work immediately without code changes.
  • Compact View (RawProfiles: false, default): Groups endpoints by canonical family and surfaces reasoning effort levels.
  • Raw View (RawProfiles: true): Exposes all raw backend endpoints and variants.
  • Custom Aliases & Resolvers: Map custom shorthand names (e.g. "fast" -> "gemini-3.8-flash-low") or inject a custom ModelResolver function in loomantigravity.Config.
provider, _ := loomantigravity.NewProvider(&loomantigravity.Config{
    TokenProvider: oauthProvider,
    Aliases: map[string]string{
        "fast": "gemini-3.8-flash-low",
        "smart": "gemini-2.5-pro",
    },
})

docs.title: 4. Quota & Rate Limit Inspection (llm.QuotaProvider)
docs.text:
The Antigravity provider implements Loom's llm.QuotaProvider interface. Quotas are decoupled from the 1-hour profile metadata cache to ensure fresh reporting without staleness:

// Assert llm.QuotaProvider
if qp, ok := provider.(llm.QuotaProvider); ok {
    // Check quota for a specific model (resolves aliases automatically)
    if quota, found, err := qp.GetQuota(ctx, "gemini-3.8-flash"); found && err == nil {
        fmt.Printf("Remaining: %.1f%%\n", quota.Percentage())
        if reset, err := quota.ParsedResetTime(); err == nil && !reset.IsZero() {
            fmt.Printf("Replenishes at: %s\n", reset.Format(time.RFC3339))
        }
    }

    // List all model quotas
    quotas, _ := qp.ListQuotas(ctx)
    for modelID, q := range quotas {
        fmt.Printf("• %-30s | Remaining: %5.1f%%\n", modelID, q.Percentage())
    }
}

docs.title: Cache Configuration
docs.text: Quota caching can be tuned in loomantigravity.Config: - QuotaCacheTTL: 30 * time.Second (Default): Avoids redundant network roundtrips during rapid polling. - QuotaCacheTTL: -1: Bypasses the cache and always executes direct live network queries. - Direct uncached queries can also be executed via provider.Client().FetchQuotas(ctx).

docs.title: 5. Token Counting & Metrics (llm.TokenCounter)
docs.text: The Antigravity provider implements Loom's llm.TokenCounter interface and provides comprehensive token metrics during streaming:

docs.title: Pre-call Token Counting (CountTokens)
docs.text:
Computes exact token counts for message sequences using Google Cloud Code's /v1internal:countTokens endpoint. If network or server issues occur, it gracefully falls back to llm.ApproximateTokenCounter:

// Assert llm.TokenCounter
if counter, ok := provider.(llm.TokenCounter); ok {
    msgs := message.MessageList{
        message.NewSystemText("You are an expert Go developer."),
        message.NewUserText("Explain channels in Go."),
    }
    count, err := counter.CountTokens(ctx, msgs)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("Total tokens: %d\n", count)
}

This enables seamless integration with Loom's memory.Summarizer and conversational memory pruning.

docs.title: Streaming Token Metrics
docs.text: The provider extracts detailed token usage from UsageMetadata chunks: - chunk.Metrics.TotalTokens: Total tokens. - chunk.Metrics.Tokens.Input: Prompt / input token count. - chunk.Metrics.Tokens.Output: Candidate completion token count. - chunk.Metrics.Tokens.CacheRead: Tokens served from Google's cached content (cachedContentTokenCount). - chunk.Metrics.Tokens.Reasoning: Reasoning / thinking tokens generated by the model (thoughtsTokenCount).

docs.title: 6. CLI Test Runner
docs.text:
The repository includes a ready-to-run interactive CLI test runner at examples/antigravity:

# 1. Authenticate via Google OAuth
go run ./examples/antigravity --login

# 2. Inspect available models and remaining quotas
go run ./examples/antigravity --list-models

# 3. View raw endpoints
go run ./examples/antigravity --list-models --raw

# 4. Check detailed quota and reset windows
go run ./examples/antigravity --quota

# 5. Count tokens for a prompt using the server endpoint
go run ./examples/antigravity --count-tokens "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."

# 6. Run a prompt with thinking effort and inspect token metrics
go run ./examples/antigravity --model gemini-3.8-flash --effort high --prompt "Analyze the complexity of QuickSort."

docs.title: Google Gemini Provider 🔌
docs.text: The Google Gemini provider (GenAI) supports Gemini 1.5 Pro, Flash, and Gemini 2.0 models.

docs.title: 1. Setup & Authentication
docs.text:
Set the GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable.

export GOOGLE_API_KEY='your-api-key-here'

docs.title: 2. Basic Usage
docs.text:
import (
    "context"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/llm"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/genai"
)

ctx := context.Background()
provider, err := loomgenai.NewDefaultProvider(ctx)
if err != nil {
    // handle error
}

model := llm.NewModel(provider, "gemini-1.5-pro")

docs.title: Reasoning
docs.text:
Configure thinking levels for models that support it.

model = model.WithThinking(2000)

docs.title: Context Caching
docs.text: Google Gemini supports long-lived context caches for large datasets or documents. Unlike Anthropic's implicit markers, Gemini caches must be explicitly created and referenced by ID.

docs.title: 1. Creating a Cache
docs.text:
You can use model.CreateCache to upload content and get a cache ID.

cacheID, _ := model.
    WithExtension(loomgenai.CacheCreation{
        DisplayName: "Project Docs",
        TTL:         1 * time.Hour,
    }).
    CreateCache(ctx, documentMessages)

docs.title: 2. Using the Cache
docs.text:
Pass the ID back using the ContextCache extension.

resp, _ := model.Invoke(ctx, prompt, llm.WithExtensionOption(loomgenai.ContextCache{ID: cacheID}))

docs.title: 3. Deleting the Cache
docs.text:
It is good practice to delete the cache when finished to save on costs.

model.DeleteCache(ctx, cacheID)

docs.title: 4. Model Profiles
docs.text:
Google provider models are statically defined and include information about multimodal support and context window sizes.

profiles := provider.SearchProfiles("gemini-1.5")

docs.title: 5. Embedding Models 🧭
docs.text:
loomgenai.Provider implements the embedding.Provider interface, supporting both text and multimodal embeddings (such as gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-2), task-type optimization, and configurable output dimensionality:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/embedding"
    loomgenai "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/genai"
)

ctx := context.Background()
provider, err := loomgenai.NewDefaultProvider(ctx)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

embedModel, err := embedding.NewModel(provider, "gemini-embedding-001", nil)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

vec, err := embedModel.
    WithDimensions(768).
    EmbedQuery(ctx, "What are the key capabilities of Gemini?")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("Vector dimensions: %d\n", vec.Dimension())

docs.title: Ollama Provider 🔌
docs.text: The Ollama provider allows you to run open-source models (like Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen) locally on your machine.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text:
Ollama must be installed and running on your system. You can download it from ollama.com.

By default, Loom connects to the standard Ollama API at http://localhost:11434.

docs.title: 2. Basic Usage
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/llm"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/ollama"
)

provider, err := loomollama.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    // handle error
}

// Make sure you have pulled the model locally: ollama pull llama3.1
model := llm.NewModel(provider, "llama3.1")

docs.title: 3. Local Model Catalog
docs.text:
Unlike cloud providers, Ollama's available models depend on what you have installed locally. You can register your local models with Loom to ensure context window metadata is available:

provider.OverrideProfile("my-local-llama", profile.Profile{
    ID: "my-local-llama",
    DisplayName: "Local Llama 3",
    Limits: profile.Limits{
        Context: 8192,
    },
})

docs.title: 4. Decision Models (System One) ⚖️
docs.text:
loomollama.Provider natively implements the decision.Provider interface, communicating directly with Ollama's /v1/systemone endpoint. This enables fast, fully local probabilistic evaluation using System One decision models such as nimble, clef, or clef-flash.

You can pass the Ollama provider directly to decision.NewModel:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/decision"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/ollama"
)

// 1. Create Ollama provider (connects to http://localhost:11434 by default)
provider, err := loomollama.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// 2. Instantiate decision model (e.g., nimble, clef, or clef-flash)
decisionModel, err := decision.NewModel(provider, "nimble", nil)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// 3. Fast local decision check
input := decision.Text("Customer says: 'Can you provide the API documentation for webhook signatures?'")
ans, err := decisionModel.Check(context.Background(), input, "Is this request asking for technical documentation?")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

if ans.Passed(0.75) {
    fmt.Printf("Technical inquiry confirmed (probability: %.2f, confidence: %.2f)\n", ans.Probability, ans.Confidence)
}

Calls to Ollama SystemOne endpoints automatically record OpenTelemetry client spans decorated with ollama.api.type = "systemone".

docs.title: 5. Embedding Models 🧭
docs.text:
loomollama.Provider natively implements the embedding.Provider interface via Ollama's /api/embed endpoint, allowing you to generate embeddings locally with models like nomic-embed-text, mxbai-embed-large, or bge-m3:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/embedding"
    loomollama "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/ollama"
)

provider, err := loomollama.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Make sure you have pulled the embedding model locally: ollama pull nomic-embed-text
embedModel, err := embedding.NewModel(provider, "nomic-embed-text", nil)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

vecs, err := embedModel.EmbedDocuments(context.Background(), []string{
    "First local document chunk",
    "Second local document chunk",
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("Embedded %d documents (dim=%d)\n", len(vecs), vecs[0].Dimension())

Calls to Ollama embedding endpoints automatically record OpenTelemetry client spans decorated with ollama.api.type = "embed".

docs.title: OpenAI Provider 🔌
docs.text: The OpenAI provider allows you to use all standard GPT models, including reasoning models like o1 and o3-mini, as well as standard models like gpt-4o.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Ensure you have the Loom package installed:

go get github.com/masterkeysrd/loom

docs.title: 2. Setup & Authentication
docs.text:
The OpenAI provider uses the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable for authentication by default.

export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key-here'

docs.title: 3. Basic Usage
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/llm"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/openai"
)

// Create the provider
provider, err := loomopenai.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    // handle error
}

// Instantiate a model
model := llm.NewModel(provider, "gpt-4o")

docs.title: Reasoning Models (Thinking)
docs.text:
For models like o1 or o3-mini that support internal reasoning, you can configure the thinking effort.

model = model.WithThinkingEffort("medium") // low, medium, high

docs.title: Structured Output
docs.text:
OpenAI's native JSON Schema enforcement is supported.

model = model.WithStructuredOutput(myJsonSchema)

docs.title: Prompt Caching
docs.text: OpenAI automatically caches prompt prefixes longer than 1024 tokens. Loom allows you to optimize this behavior using the PromptCache extension:

docs.title: 1. Cache Bucketing (Key)
docs.text:
Use a stable identifier to improve cache hit rates by bucketing similar requests together.

model = model.WithExtension(loomopenai.PromptCache{
    Key: "user-session-123",
})

docs.title: 2. Extended Retention
docs.text:
By default, caches are ephemeral. You can enable extended caching (up to 24 hours) for specific prefixes.

model = model.WithExtension(loomopenai.PromptCache{
    Retention: "24h",
})

docs.title: 5. Model Catalog
docs.text:
The provider includes a static catalog of common OpenAI models with their context limits and capabilities. You can search or list them at runtime:

profiles := provider.ListProfiles()
for _, p := range profiles {
    fmt.Printf("Model: %s, Context: %d\n", p.ID, p.Limits.Context)
}

docs.title: 6. Decision Models (System One) ⚖️
docs.text:
loomopenai.Provider natively implements the decision.Provider interface, communicating directly with OpenAI's /v1/decisions endpoint. This allows you to evaluate fast, calibrated probabilistic questions using decision models such as gpt-6-luna.

You can pass the OpenAI provider directly to decision.NewModel:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/decision"
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/openai"
)

// 1. Create OpenAI provider
provider, err := loomopenai.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// 2. Instantiate decision model (e.g., gpt-6-luna)
decisionModel, err := decision.NewModel(provider, "gpt-6-luna", nil)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// 3. Fast probabilistic predicate check
input := decision.Text("Order #1294: Expedited overnight delivery to an unverified address with a new credit card.")
ans, err := decisionModel.Check(context.Background(), input, "Is this order high-risk fraud?")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

if ans.Passed(0.80) {
    fmt.Printf("Flagged for fraud review (probability: %.2f, confidence: %.2f)\n", ans.Probability, ans.Confidence)
}

Calls to OpenAI decisions automatically record OpenTelemetry client spans decorated with openai.api.type = "decisions".

docs.title: 7. Embedding Models 🧭
docs.text:
loomopenai.Provider also implements the embedding.Provider interface for generating dense text embeddings using models like text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large:

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/embedding"
    loomopenai "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/openai"
)

provider, err := loomopenai.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

embedModel, err := embedding.NewModel(provider, "text-embedding-3-small", nil)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Optionally reduce vector dimensions (e.g., 512)
embedModel = embedModel.WithDimensions(512)

vec, err := embedModel.EmbedQuery(context.Background(), "How does Loom handle state persistence?")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("Vector dimensions: %d\n", vec.Dimension())

Calls to OpenAI embeddings automatically record OpenTelemetry client spans decorated with openai.api.type = "embeddings".

docs.title: TypeSafe AI Provider ⚖️
docs.text:
The TypeSafe AI provider (loomtypesafe) offers native, high-performance integration with TypeSafe AI's dedicated System One / Decision Model API.

Unlike general-purpose generative LLM providers, TypeSafe AI is purpose-built specifically for ultra-fast, calibrated probabilistic decisions, binary predicates, categorical classification, and ordinal scoring.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
TypeSafe AI provides dedicated System One endpoints: - Evaluation: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone - Model Discovery: GET https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/models

loomtypesafe.Provider natively implements both decision.Provider and profile.Provider, allowing it to be plugged directly into decision.NewModel without any adapter.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Ultra-low latency & cost: Purpose-built decision inference at $0.042 per 1M input tokens ($0 output tokens).
  • Automatic payload compression: Payloads $\ge$ 1 KiB are automatically gzip-compressed by default.
  • Resilient retries: Built-in exponential backoff on HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and 529 Overloaded.
  • Dynamic model catalog: Models and profiles are queryable via provider.ListModels(ctx).
  • Extended context extension: Context limits can be scaled from 64k up to 262k tokens via loomtypesafe.LongContext.

docs.title: 2. Setup & Authentication
docs.text:
The TypeSafe AI provider uses the TYPESAFE_API_KEY environment variable for authentication:

export TYPESAFE_API_KEY='your-typesafe-api-key'
# Optional: override default API endpoint (https://api.typesafe.ai)
export TYPESAFE_BASE_URL='https://api.typesafe.ai'

docs.title: Default Provider
docs.text:
Reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY and optional TYPESAFE_BASE_URL from the environment:

import (
    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/decision"
    loomtypesafe "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/typesafe"
)

provider, err := loomtypesafe.NewDefaultProvider()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

docs.title: Custom Provider Options
docs.text:
Use functional options to configure the client:

provider, err := loomtypesafe.NewProvider(
    loomtypesafe.WithAPIKey("ts-custom-key"),
    loomtypesafe.WithBaseURL("https://api.typesafe.ai"),
    loomtypesafe.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}),
    loomtypesafe.WithCompression(true), // Enabled by default for payloads >= 1 KiB
    loomtypesafe.WithMaxRetries(5),      // Exponential backoff for 429/529 (default: 3)
)

Available options: - WithAPIKey(string): Sets the API key. - WithBaseURL(string): Overrides the base URL (defaults to https://api.typesafe.ai). - WithHTTPClient(*http.Client): Injects a custom HTTP client. - WithCompression(bool): Controls automatic gzip compression for requests $\ge$ 1 KiB (enabled by default). - WithMaxRetries(int): Sets the maximum number of retries on 429 (Too Many Requests) or 529 (Overloaded) responses (default: 3).

docs.title: 4. Models & Pricing
docs.text:
TypeSafe AI models specialize in deterministic probability calibration:

Model Constant Model ID Description Context Limit Input Price / 1M loomtypesafe.ModelJevLatest "jev-latest" Recommended stable alias (points to jev-1.13.0) 64k (262k with extension) $0.042 loomtypesafe.ModelJevPreview "jev-preview" Preview release alias (points to jev-1.14.0) 64k (262k with extension) $0.042 loomtypesafe.ModelJev1_14_0 "jev-1.14.0" Pin to specific version 1.14.0 64k (262k with extension) $0.042 loomtypesafe.ModelJev1_13_0 "jev-1.13.0" Pin to specific version 1.13.0 64k (262k with extension) $0.042

docs.title: Dynamic Model Discovery
docs.text:
You can query the TypeSafe AI catalog at runtime via ListModels:

models, err := provider.ListModels(ctx)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

for _, m := range models {
    fmt.Printf("Model: %-15s Released: %s (%s)\n", m.Name, m.ReleaseDate, m.Description)
}

docs.title: 5. Supported Question Types
docs.text:
TypeSafe AI natively supports all three core decision question types:

  1. Binary Predicate (decision.Predicate):
  2. Maps to TypeSafe AI's "noul" question type.
  3. Supports explicit criteria via .WithCriteria(trueDesc, falseDesc).
  4. Categorical Choice (decision.Choice):
  5. Maps to TypeSafe AI's "choice" question type.
  6. Supports up to 255 discrete options.
  7. Ordinal Score (decision.Score):
  8. Maps to TypeSafe AI's "score" question type.
  9. Evaluates across 2 to 10 rubric levels.

[!WARNING] Modality Support: TypeSafe AI is optimized for pure text and structured JSON state (decision.Text and decision.State). It does not accept multimodal image inputs. For visual evaluations, use the OpenAI Decisions provider or the LLM fallback adapter.

docs.title: 6. Danger Zone: Long Context Extension
docs.text:
By default, TypeSafe AI enforces a 64k token limit per request (with up to 32k tokens per question).

To evaluate large documents, legal contracts, or extensive conversation transcripts, enable the LongContext extension. This sends the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true header to elevate context capacity to 262k tokens:

docs.title: Model-Level Configuration
docs.text:
// Enable long context for all calls made by this model
model = model.WithExtension(loomtypesafe.LongContext{Enabled: true})

docs.title: Call-Level Configuration
docs.text:
// Enable long context for a single evaluation request
resp, err := model.EvaluateWithOptions(
    ctx,
    decision.Text(hugeDocument),
    questions,
    decision.WithExtensionOption(loomtypesafe.LongContext{Enabled: true}),
)

docs.title: 7. Basic Usage Example
docs.text:
Here is a complete example demonstrating single-question checks and batch evaluations:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/decision"
    loomtypesafe "github.com/masterkeysrd/loom/providers/typesafe"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // 1. Initialize the TypeSafe AI provider
    provider, err := loomtypesafe.NewDefaultProvider()
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Failed to initialize TypeSafe provider: %v", err)
    }

    // 2. Instantiate a decision model using jev-latest
    model, err := decision.NewModel(provider, loomtypesafe.ModelJevLatest, nil)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Failed to create decision model: %v", err)
    }

    // 3. Single-question shortcut: Check (Predicate)
    input := decision.Text("Customer states: 'I never authorized this $450 transaction on my card.'")
    ans, err := model.Check(ctx, input, "Is this a fraud or unauthorized transaction dispute?")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    if ans.Passed(0.80) {
        fmt.Printf("Dispute flagged (probability: %.2f, confidence: %.2f)\n", 
            ans.Probability, ans.Confidence)
    }

    // 4. Batch evaluation with Predicate, Choice, and Score
    orderState := struct {
        Amount   float64 `json:"amount"`
        Shipping string  `json:"shipping"`
        NewUser  bool    `json:"new_user"`
    }{
        Amount:   1299.99,
        Shipping: "International Courier",
        NewUser:  true,
    }

    resp, err := model.Evaluate(ctx, decision.State(orderState),
        decision.Predicate("high_value", "Is this an unusually high-value order?").
            WithCriteria("Amount exceeds $1,000", "Amount is under $1,000"),
        decision.Choice("action", "Select the recommended review action",
            decision.Opt("approve", "Auto-approve order"),
            decision.Opt("hold", "Hold for verification"),
            decision.Opt("reject", "Reject transaction"),
        ),
        decision.Score("risk", "Rate transaction risk level",
            decision.Lvl("low", "Normal risk pattern"),
            decision.Lvl("medium", "Elevated risk pattern"),
            decision.Lvl("high", "Critical risk pattern"),
        ),
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    if a, ok := resp.Answer("action"); ok {
        fmt.Printf("Selected Action: %s (confidence: %.2f)\n", a.Choice, a.Confidence)
    }
    if s, ok := resp.Answer("risk"); ok {
        fmt.Printf("Risk Score: %.2f (normalized: %.2f)\n", s.Score, s.NormalizedScore())
    }
}
